To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a method to estimate the functional connectivity in neuronal cultures recorded by a high-density CMOS-MEA, and we applied it to characterize the connectivity of sparse neuronal cultures at single cell level.

we have developed and tested a method that permits the estimation of effective connections in neuronal networks recorded by high-density MEAs at high temporal and spatial resolution, and that we have applied this method on sparse neuronal networks to infer the effective connectivity and to compare the obtained results with the network structure inferred from staining procedures.

we could demonstrate that the combination of a high spatial resolution CMOS-MEA with a novel spatio-temporal cross-correlation based method allows the estimation of effective functional connectivity in sparse neuronal networks at the single cell level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to analyze the effective functional connectivity among neurons recorded by MEAs.
a new method for the analysis of neuronal cultures recorded with high-density MEAs.
the estimation of functional connectivity from high spatial and temporal resolution electrophysiological data, and with the analysis of its dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method is able to detect and quantify the functional connectivity of neuronal networks with a high degree of accuracy and reliability, even at cellular resolution.
the proposed approach is a powerful tool for the analysis of functional connectivity in sparse neuronal cultures recorded by CMOS-MEAs.

the proposed approach, when applied to the data recorded by the high density CMOS-MEA, allows to infer functional connections in low-density neuronal networks with high spatial resolution and to obtain a detailed characterization of the inferred links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new approach for the analysis of the functional effective connectivity on low density neuronal cultures.

the combination of the high-resolution MEA recordings with the proposed method allows to obtain detailed maps of functional connections in sparse cultures and that the proposed method is a valuable tool to analyze neuronal networks in vitro and in vivo.

we have demonstrated that the proposed approach is suitable for the estimation of functional connections at high spatial and temporal resolution, allowing to discriminate between possible causality and spurious coactivations, and to obtain a detailed map of the network at cellular resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to infer functional connections in low-density neuronal cultures, and to obtain information about the underlying network structure and its dynamics.
the proposed approach allows to infer functional connectivity in sparse neuronal cultures recorded by CMOS MEA devices.

the use of high-density CMOS MEAs and the application of spatio-temporal analysis of neuronal cultures recorded by these devices can lead to the estimation of functional effective connectivity with a high spatial and temporal resolution.
